chunks: And by this chain, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Ibrāhīm al-Jaʿfarī, who said:

Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Ḥasan wrote to Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar (عليه السلام): As for what follows, I exhort myself to taqwā of Allah, and by it I exhort you, for it is Allah’s counsel to the former ones and His counsel to the later ones. Those who came to me from among Allah’s helpers upon His religion and the spread of His obedience informed me of your tenderness together with your abandonment. I had consulted concerning the call to al-Riḍā from the family of Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وآله), but you concealed it, and your father concealed it before you. Long ago you claimed what was not yours, and extended your hopes toward what Allah did not give you; so you followed desire and led astray. And I am warning you of what Allah warned you against from Himself.

So Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) wrote to him: From Mūsā son of Abī ʿAbdillāh Jaʿfar and ʿAlī, both sharing in humility before Allah and obedience to Him, to Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn Ḥasan. As for what follows, I warn you by Allah and myself, and inform you of the painfulness of His punishment, the severity of His retribution, and the full measure of His vengeance. And I exhort you and myself to taqwā of Allah, for it is the adornment of speech and the stabilization of blessings.

Your letter reached me, in which you mention that I am a claimant, and my father before me, though you did not hear that from me. Their testimony will be written and they will be questioned. The greed of this world and its pursuits leaves for its people no pursuit for their Hereafter without corrupting for them the pursuit of their Hereafter within their worldly life.

And you mentioned that I held people back from you out of desire for what is in your hands. Had I desired that into which you have entered, what kept me from it would not have been weakness regarding a sunnah nor lack of insight concerning a proof. Rather, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, created people as mixed kinds, with differing peculiarities and instincts. So inform me about two expressions that I ask you about: what is al-ʿatraf in your body, and what is al-ṣahlaj in the human being?

Then write to me with news of that. I am sending ahead to you a warning against disobeying the caliph, and urging you toward dutifulness and obedience to him, and that you seek safety for yourself before the claws seize you and strangulation closes upon you from every place, so that you seek relief and breath from every side and do not find it, until Allah bestows upon you by His favor and grace, and by the compassion of the caliph—may Allah preserve him—so that he may grant you safety, have mercy on you, and preserve in you the kinship ties of the Messenger of Allah. Peace be upon whoever follows guidance.
Indeed, it has been revealed to us that the punishment is upon whoever denies and turns away.

Al-Jaʿfarī said: It reached me that the letter of Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) fell into the hands of Hārūn. When he read it, he said: The people are inciting me against Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar, while he is innocent of what he is accused of.

key_terms.الدَّعْوَةِ: the call or summons to a leadership claim
key_terms.الرِّضَا: the one approved from the family of Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وآله), in the context of political-religious claim
key_terms.الْعَذَابَ: punishment for denial and turning away
key_terms.الْهُدَىٰ: guidance, in the closing formula of peace
key_terms.تَقْوَى اللَّهِ: God-consciousness and piety, presented as divine counsel and the basis of right conduct
key_terms.تَكَامُلَ نَقِمَاتِهِ: the full completion of divine acts of vengeance or retribution
key_terms.مُدَّعٍ: a claimant; one accused of making a claim

ai.seo_question: What does the letter of Imam Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) to Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbdullāh say about leadership claims and obedience to authority?
ai.summary: This report preserves an exchange between Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbdullāh and Imam Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) concerning claims to leadership, taqwā, and political conduct. The Imam’s reply rejects false accusation, warns against worldly ambition, and counsels restraint and avoidance of confrontation, while concluding with a Qur’anic declaration about punishment for those who deny and turn away.
